text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"NJ","level":"state","category":"security_deposits","status":"in_force","title":"NJ Security Deposit Law: interest-bearing accounts, notices and 30-day return","requirement":"Security deposits may not be commingled with the landlord's personal property. They must be held in an interest-bearing account at an insured New Jersey bank or savings and loan (landlords with 10 or more units may instead use an insured money market fund of a NJ-based investment company or a variable-rate account). Interest belongs to the tenant and is paid in cash or credited to rent on the lease renewal/anniversary or January 31. The landlord must give written notice of the bank, amount, account type and interest rate within 30 days of receipt and at each annual interest payment, and within 30 days of any transfer. Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest less itemized deductions, sent by personal delivery or registered/certified mail. Within 5 business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation, the landlord must return the deposit. A new owner is responsible for the deposit and interest.","key_value":"Return within 30 days of tenancy termination (5 business days if displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation); interest paid to tenant; 7% per annum applied if notice or interest requirements are not met","coverage_conditions":"Residential tenancies in New Jersey.
